name: single_web

input.offline_required: fixtures object keyed by canonical HTTPS URL, each containing body string and optional status and headers
input.fixture_encoding: Fixture body strings are encoded as UTF-8; fixture Content-Type should declare UTF-8.
input.limits: timeout_seconds (0.01-60 total cooperative deadline), max_bytes (1-5000000 per response), max_redirects (0-10 per source), top_k (1-50)

tested_scope: Offline captured HTML ingestion and query-dependent lexical passage ranking
HTML entities, inline text, ignored head/script/style/template text and bounded passage chunks
Explicit exact hostname allowlist; HTTPS-only URLs; no credentials, IP literals, fragments, alternate ports, controls or ambiguous authorities
Relative redirects, final URL citations, denied redirect destinations, loop and hop limits
Duplicate source IDs and unsafe source URLs rejected before any fetch
Explicit content-type, encoding, byte limit, timeout, HTTP error, missing fixture and no-match failures
Optional injected synthesis checks citation URLs and verbatim quotes against selected passages
Public-address DNS filtering, pinned address connection and original-host TLS SNI using mocks
urllib response reading, redirect suppression, size limits and timeout translation using mocks; real HTTPResponse parsing against an in-memory HTTP wire fixture
Offline JSON CLI success and structured error output

retrieval.algorithm: Unicode word tokenization, case-folded OR query matching, TF/IDF-style lexical scoring with a small length penalty; deterministic top-k passages
retrieval.citation_contract: Each extracted quote has a source ID and final validated URL. Synthesis citations must use those exact URLs and nonempty verbatim substrings of selected evidence.
retrieval.adapter: urllib HTTPS with default verified TLS, environment proxies disabled, automatic redirects disabled, public DNS addresses pinned to sockets; engine validates every manual redirect

limitations: No live web retrieval was performed; supplied demonstration fixtures are authored offline examples, not claimed live captures.
Live HTTPS behavior is exercised with mocked transport/DNS only; live interoperability is not verified.
Injected fetchers and synthesizers are trusted in-process code and must cooperate with deadlines; synchronous callbacks cannot be forcibly interrupted.
DNS waiting is bounded, but an operating-system resolver worker cannot be killed and may delay interpreter shutdown after timeout.

Socket timeouts and deadline checks bound network waits and body reads; extraction/ranking checks the deadline after bounded parsing rather than preempting CPU work. HTTP header parsing is not a hard process-level wall-clock deadline.
The urllib body socket access uses CPython response internals and may need adjustment on alternate Python runtimes.
Only uncompressed HTML/XHTML is supported. No JavaScript execution, cookies, authentication, robots.txt policy enforcement, PDF parsing, crawling or search-engine discovery.
Extraction is lightweight HTML parsing, not browser rendering; CSS-hidden content and navigation may remain, and malformed markup may lose text.
Ranking is lexical rather than semantic and can return a passage matching only one query term.
Source citations prove quoted text was present in retrieved evidence, not that evidence is true or that all synthesized claims are supported. No LLM provider calls are included.
Requests fail as a whole on any source failure; duplicate IDs are forbidden but distinct IDs may reference the same URL.
measurement: No token counts, costs, provider usage or client outcomes are estimated by this build.
